Question 4

Consider the differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}=6 x^{2}-x^{2} y\). Let \(y=f(x)\) be a particular solution to this differential equation with the initial condition \(f(-1)=2\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Use Euler's method with two steps of equal size, starting at \(x=-1\), to approximate \(f(0)\). Show the work that leads to your answer.
\item[(b)] At the point \((-1,2)\), the value of \(\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}\) is -12. Find the second-degree Taylor polynomial for \(f\) about \(x=-1\).
\item[(c)] Find the particular solution \(y=f(x)\) to the given differential equation with the initial condition \(f(-1)=2\).
\item[(a)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
f\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) & \approx f(-1)+\left(\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{(-1,2)}\right) \cdot \Delta x \\
& =2+4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}=4
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(0) & \approx f\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)+\left(\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{\left(-\frac{1}{2}, 4\right)}\right) \cdot \Delta x \\
& \approx 4+\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2}=\frac{17}{4}
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)] \(P_{2}(x)=2+4(x+1)-6(x+1)^{2}\)
\item[(c)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{d y}{d x}=x^{2}(6-y) \\
& \int \frac{1}{6-y} d y=\int x^{2} d x \\
& -\ln |6-y|=\frac{1}{3} x^{3}+C \\
& -\ln 4=-\frac{1}{3}+C \\
& C=\frac{1}{3}-\ln 4 \\
& \ln |6-y|=-\frac{1}{3} x^{3}-\left(\frac{1}{3}-\ln 4\right) \\
& |6-y|=4 e^{-\frac{1}{3}\left(x^{3}+1\right)} \\
& y=6-4 e^{-\frac{1}{3}\left(x^{3}+1\right)}
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[2] : \(\left\{\begin{array}{l}1 \text { : Euler's method with two steps } \\ 1 \text { : answer }\end{array}\right.\)

\end{itemize}
